name: Evergy
description: Evergy is a holding company for vertically integrated electric utilities (Evergy Kansas Central, Evergy Metro and Evergy Missouri West) that generate, transmit and sell electricity to about 1.7 million customers in Kansas and Missouri (1.5 million homes, 0.2 million businesses and 7,400 industrials, municipalities and other utilities). Kansas and Missouri regulators set retail rates to recover cost plus a return on the capital invested, so earnings grow as the company adds rate base, and the company reports as a single segment. About 81% of revenue is retail electricity, 9% is transmission and 5% wholesale; in 2026 it signed electric service agreements with data-center customers totalling about 2,600 MW of projected peak load.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Utilities' and Sub-Industry 'Electric Utilities' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 4931 (Electric & Other Services Combined) per EDGAR.

hq.note: EDGAR business address: Kansas City, MO; Wikipedia S&P 500 list also Kansas City, Missouri

employees.note: Evergy Companies; 2,479 represented by IBEW and other local unions (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Retail electric
businessLines.how: Customers pay state-approved tariffs monthly (about one-third of retail revenue falls in the third quarter); fuel and purchased power are largely recovered, and profit is the allowed return on the rate base.
businessLines.description: Residential, commercial and industrial electricity sales in Kansas and Missouri, 42,919 thousand MWh sold in 2025.

businessLines.name: Transmission
businessLines.how: Network transmission customers pay regulated formula rates set by FERC that recover cost plus a return on the transmission rate base.
businessLines.description: Revenue from the use of Evergy's transmission system in the SPP.

businessLines.how: Priced at market in the SPP, so earnings vary with market prices and plant availability, with retail customers sharing margins under regulatory rules.
businessLines.description: Sales of power not needed for retail load, mainly into the SPP Integrated Marketplace.
